analysis: All three converge on PostgreSQL with technically sound justification (CTEs, window functions, ACID consistency, read replicas, materialized views), so quality is high across the board. The differentiator is correction durability. System A is strongest: it proactively recalls that DynamoDB and MongoDB were already evaluated and rejected, cites the team's existing PostgreSQL expertise and primary-DB status, and adds extension-based scaling (TimescaleDB) — answering as if the prior corrections persisted. System B is nearly as good operationally and never resurfaces the rejected options, but doesn't explicitly anchor to the past decision. System C explicitly states it has no stored knowledge and then re-debates MongoDB/DynamoDB and floats a ClickHouse sidecar — the classic vanilla pattern that forces the user to re-spend correction tokens, so it ranks last despite a competent final recommendation.
